pack.description: Worked example manifest: service-desk operational friction composed entirely from platform primitives over normalised concepts. Ships no code.

certification.notes: Submitted for Partner review against the 2.0 platform.

detectors.title: Repeated manual resolution of the same incident shape

labels.summary: The same resolution is applied repeatedly by hand.
labels.whyItMatters: Repeated identical resolutions are the clearest candidate for an assisting agent.
labels.recommendation: An agent handles the recurring cases; the residual requires judgment.

labels.summary: Open incidents are ageing well past the queue's normal dwell time.

detectors.title: Incidents concentrate on a shared dependency

labels.summary: Incidents across several services concentrate on one shared dependency.
labels.evidenceHint: Concentration only — the finding never asserts causation.

detectors.title: Alerts consistently pair with a raised incident

labels.summary: Alerts are followed by a manually raised incident inside the correlation window.

glossary.incident: A tracked service-desk record representing a disruption reported by a user.
glossary.queue: A named work list a group of agents draws from.
glossary.dwell_time: Elapsed time an incident spends in its current state.

terminology.llmContext: Service-desk operations analysis. Speak service-desk language: incidents, queues, dwell time, escalation. Reference groups and queues only, never individuals. Describe concentration, never causation. No automated incident resolution: humans remain responsible for every action.
